source: Google Maps local list view (free browser extraction, no paid API)
limitation: Google Maps list view does not expose review counts in this layout. Supply strength is therefore expressed as operator count, median rating and website presence only. Review depth requires the paid Places API.

region_legend.core: Evan's backyard - Duval, Jacksonville Beach, St Johns, Clay, Nassau
region_legend.fringe: NE Florida outer ring, still drivable
region_legend.out: out-of-area comparison metros (GA/FL interior/NC/SC) - not prospects

boat detailing.why: Mobile-first work with no shop requirement; core-river metros (Fleming Island, Orange Park, Middleburg, Amelia, Yulee) are thin on boat-only operators while the beaches are saturated at 5.0. The visible supply in most core metros is car detailers with a boat line.

well pump repair.why: Deepest supply gap in the drivable ring. Orange Park returned 2 listings, Macclenny 3.0-3.2-rated shops, and a large share of core/fringe operators have no website at all (Destin's, Williams, Smitty's, Mumford, Mizell, The Pump Guy, St Johns Well). 24-hour flags are common, which reads as intake gap, not visibility gap.

hurricane shutter installation.why: One true specialist (First Coast Hurricane Shutters) serves the whole core; every other result is a blinds store or window installer. Orange Park: 2 results. Consultative sale, so the sellable product is qualified appointments, not intake.

marine salvage / recovery.why: 2-3 results per metro and no dedicated marine salvage operator in any scanned metro - only dive shops and tow services. Genuine availability gap, but storm-gated: a burst business, best run as the surge-brokering adjunct.

septic tank pumping.why: 7-11 operators per metro at 4.3-5.0, nearly all with websites. No visibility gap anywhere in the ring. Only the after-hours intake angle survives.

dock / marine construction.why: 7-10 per metro, median 4.9-5.0, websites near-universal. Premium trade with established relationships; not a lead-gen opening.

porta potty rental.why: Heavy listing density, but a large share are unrated, no-website, city-name shell listings - the SEO-spam pattern. Real operators (Floaters, Premier, Fortis, Maxline, Carefree) are established. Not a clean gap.

generator repair.why: 5-7 per metro, mostly electricians and generator dealers rather than repair specialists. Moderate opening at best; storm-season demand spike is real but seasonal.

land clearing.why: 5-8 per metro at 5.0, developer-led with long sales cycles. Not a call-driven business.

mobile mechanic.why: 7 per metro, 24-hour flags everywhere, several no-website operators. Density is high enough that this is a service-quality competition, not a supply gap.

paid_pull.what: review counts (Google Places via serper, 7 calls) + keyword volume/CPC (Serpstat, 20 terms)
corrects: Well pump has established incumbents (median 132 reviews); the gap is geographic, not metro-wide.
Boat detailing has the thinnest bench (median 17 reviews).
Jacksonville-specific search demand is 10-70/mo in all four trades, so a lead-volume product has no supply of leads.
CPC is high where volume is low ($6.27 well pump repair jacksonville, $4.17 shutters) - commercial value per click, not volume.
